title: WPMS/1267/2005 of KUNWAR M.A. KHAN Vs DISTRICT JUDGE and ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1267 of 2005 (M/S)
Kunwar M.A. Khan .....Petitioner
Versus
District Judge, Nainital and others .....Respondents
Mr. Sharad Sharma, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. J.S. Bisht, Advocate for
the petitioner.
Mr. T.S. Phartiyal, Advocate for the respondent No.3.
Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
Present petition is filed assailing the order dated
03.06.2005, passed by the J.S.C.C. / Civil Judge (S.D.)
in J.S.C.C. Suit No. 13 of 2004 whereby learned Trial
Court held that since question of title has been raised
and is involved in the suit, therefore, in view of Section
23 of the provincial Small Cause Courts Act, same
cannot be adjudicated by the J.S.C.C. and can only be
decided by the Regular Civil Court, therefore, suit is not
maintainable before the J.S.C.C.
Petitioner/landlord filed suit for recovery of rent
as well as for recovery of possession after evicting the
tenant/respondent from the property, in question. In a
suit so filed, defendant filed his written statement
specifically stating therein that plaintiff is not the owner
and landlord of the property in question, therefore,
J.S.C.C. has absolutely no jurisdiction to hear and
decide the case in view of Section 23 of the Act.
Learned Trial Court, having heard learned counsel
for the parties, was pleased to observe that since
question of title was involved in the suit, therefore, suit
was not maintainable before the J.S.C.C. and plaint was
directed to be returned to the plaintiff to present the

2
same before regular civil court. Section 23 of the
provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887 reads as
under :-
"23. Return of plaints in suits involving
questions of title.- (1) Notwithstanding
anything in the foregoing portion of this 'Act, when
the right of a plaintiff and the relief claimed by him
in a Court of Small Causes depend upon the proof
or disproof of a title to immovable property or
other title which such a Court cannot finally
determine, the Court may at any stage of the
proceedings return the plaint to be presented to a
Court having jurisdiction to determine the title.
(2) When a Court returns a plaint under sub-section (1), it shall comply with the provisions of
the second paragraph of section 57 of the Code of
Civil Procedure (14 of 1882) and make such order
with respect to costs as it deems just and the Court
shall, for the purpose of the Indian Limitation Act,
1877 (15 of 1877) be deemed to have been unable to
entertain the suit by reason of a cause of a nature
like to that of defect of jurisdiction."
Having perused Section 23 of the Act, I have no
hesitation to hold that if title of the plaintiff is disputed
by the defendant in J.S.C.C. suit, learned Judge hearing
the J.S.C.C. suit, has absolutely no other option except
to return the plaint for the presentation before the
regular civil court. However, if question of title is not
disputed and only relationship of landlord and tenant is

3
involved, then learned J.S.C.C. can decide the
relationship of landlord and tenant in J.S.C.C. suit.
Perusal of written statement demonstrates that
defendant has disputed the title of the plaintiff and has
stated that neither plaintiff is owner nor landlord of the
property. Therefore, impugned order seems to be
justified.
In view of the above, present petition lacks merit
and is hereby dismissed. However, plaint shall be
returned to the plaintiff within a week. Plaintiff shall
present the plaint within a week thereafter before the
competent Civil Court. Learned Civil Court shall decide
the same at its own merit in accordance with law at the
earliest preferably within one year from the date of
presentation. Learned Trial Court shall not grant any
unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties.
No order as to costs.
(Alok Singh, J.)
Dated 10th April, 2014 Shiv
